properties.description:
ARRIVED 2026-09-12, in two halves — epoch:the-export-chains-from-main and epoch:the-server-keeps-the-export-current. Second of the four Anthony ordered on 2026-09-11. The shared server writes the design export to the working tree after every graph change, debounced, and chains its prev_content_hash from the export as committed on the default branch rather than from whatever was last written to disk.

WHY IT WAS HERE: it removes a class of loss rather than an instance — the forgotten export — and the guarantee had to live in the server because the session is the thing that might not come back. It also made dec:export-once-per-pr automatic: chained from the merge-base, any number of commits on a branch each chain from the same ancestor, and squash-and-merge lands one hop per PR.

ALL FOUR QUESTIONS IT CARRIED ARE ANSWERED:
· THE DEBOUNCE INTERVAL — two seconds of quiet, with a ten-second ceiling so a steady stream of writes cannot starve the export forever.
· THE GIT QUERY — the MERGE-BASE with the default branch, not the tip. On a long-lived branch the tip moves underneath you and the export would claim descent from work it never contained.
· A HAND-EDITED WORKING TREE — skip the write and warn loudly, Anthony's call 2026-09-12, put to him with the two alternatives and their costs. Never destroys a hand edit or a half-resolved merge; the accepted cost is that the export stops being current until somebody reads the warning, which is why it is in loop_status' `next`.
· THE NO-GIT FALLBACK — today's on-disk chaining, reported rather than silent, so reflow2 assumes nothing about git.

ONE QUESTION THE INCREMENT DID NOT ANTICIPATE and had to settle: how the server learns WHICH file to keep current. An explicit `--export-to`, rather than deriving it from export history, which would have let one export to a scratch path silently re-target the server's writes. `reflow2_init.py` emits it for all three harnesses so a consumer opts in without knowing the flag exists.

IT DID NOT CHANGE DURABILITY, as planned. The store stays RocksDB — this makes the git RECORD reliable, it does not make the export the only copy.

NO VERSION NUMBER BY DESIGN.
properties.name: The server guarantees the export, and the lineage chains from main
